extraction.name: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu. Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. arXiv:2407.11828v4 [eess.AS], 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected through a rigorous data collection process involving 200 participants (188 retained after post-processing) who read sentences from French Wikipedia while wearing six audio sensors (five body-conduction and one airborne reference). Recordings were made in both quiet and noisy environments using a 3D sound spatializer with 56 loudspeakers. The recording protocol consists of four steps: speech-clean, speechless-noisy, speechless-clean, and speech-noisy.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data includes audio recordings from six sensors: headset microphone (Shure WH20XLR), forehead accelerometer (Knowles BU23173-000), in-ear soft foam microphone (Knowles FG-23329-P07), in-ear rigid earpiece microphone (Knowles SPH1642HT5H), throat microphone (iXradio XVTM822D-D35), and temple vibration pickup (AKG C411). Textual data originates from French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Noise samples were sourced from Audio Set and in-house ambisonic recordings.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Post-processing included three automatic filters: Phoneme Error Rate (PER) < 10%, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) > 1.5 dB, and Lspeech_50 > Lsilence_50. Voice Activity Detection timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides. Audio was trimmed by 15 ms if adjusted timestamps exceeded original boundaries. The dataset was split by speaker into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Linguistic transcriptions were obtained from French Wikipedia text, filtered to remove proper names, numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors. Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the text phonemizer of the CoML lab, with manual correction for unrecognized words. Recording conditions annotations are also included.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Whisper-timestamped model for speech-to-text and dynamic time warping; text phonemizer from CoML lab for phonetic transcription.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender, age (mean 28.55 years, range 18-82), and language (French) are collected. The dataset is GDPR-compliant with informed consent, anonymization, and encryption.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to French language. Body-conduction sensors have limited bandwidth due to low-pass filtering of tissues. Some sensors may have acoustic sealing issues depending on ear canal anatomy. The dataset may not generalize to all real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and validation for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension), speech-to-phonemes recognition, and speaker verification. Also potential for voice commands and vital sign monitoring.
